display.title: Eight Chanukah Lights: The Miracle of the First Night and a Secret Chuppah
display.summary_short: Why we light eight Chanukah lights and light them after sunset, with stories of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's vinegar candles and a secret chuppah in Soviet Russia.
display.summary_long: The storyteller asks why Chanukah has eight days when the oil was only a miracle for seven. One answer: finding even one pure jar after three years of the Greeks in the Beis HaMikdash was a miracle. Another comes from the Gemara: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's daughter lit her Shabbos candles with vinegar by mistake, and he told her that the One who commands oil to burn can command vinegar to burn. Oil burning is a miracle too; as the Baal Shem Tov taught, nature is simply a miracle that repeats, shown with the parable of a world seeing the sun rise for the first time. Next he explains why we light after sunset: Chanukah is about bringing light into darkness, and we bring others closer with warmth and a smile. The Rebbe tells a visitor how the Frierdiker Rebbe advised him to greet Jews with a hearty 'good Shabbos'. Finally, in Soviet Yekaterinoslav, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, the Rebbe's father, secretly makes a chuppah at midnight and must call up the building's informer to complete the minyan, with a surprising result.
display.lesson: Everything in nature is a miracle from Hashem, even what happens every day. Like the Chanukah lights, we chase away darkness with light: bring others close with kindness and a smile.

advisories.note: Soviet authorities jail Jews for teaching Torah and pay informers; a wedding must be held in secret.

sources_cited.note: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and the vinegar that burned (cited as 'Gemara Taanis').
